column3: Flexure block made a state variable: carry w_prev (zeros on the first call); t_load = h + w_prev is the UN-deflected rock column; q = ρc·g·t_load; k = sqrt(kx²+ky²); W = FFT2(q)/(D·k⁴ + (ρm−ρinfill)·g); w_new = IFFT2(W); h −= (w_new − w_prev); w_prev = w_new. Prose states that the naive form (load from the already-deflected h, written back over h) converges to zero at 0.15 per call, and that PLAN v1's 'compute w_new from the deflected h and subtract only the increment' converges to h₀/(1+T) = 0.54·h₀ at long wavelength, not (1−T)·h₀ = 0.15·h₀. column4: T(k) = ρc·g/(D·k⁴ + Δρ·g). Call 1: w = T·h₀, h = (1−T)·h₀. Call 2: t_load = h + w = h₀, same w, h unchanged — the fixed point is (1−T)·h₀ exactly. column4: Textual: the rewritten bullet is now consistent with the two clauses it contradicted — the shadow paragraph immediately below (casters tested against the LIGHT's frustum, never the camera's HiZ) and the failure row for shadows missing from objects the camera cannot see. column3: Two additions. (a) New paragraph after the ladder table: the small-primitive test rejects a triangle whose screen-space bounds enclose no pixel CENTRE, which is the rasterizer's rule only for single-sample, non-conservative pixels; under MSAA coverage is evaluated at SAMPLE positions so the test culls triangles that legitimately cover samples and edge AA goes ragged; under conservative rasterization any overlap of the pixel AREA counts so it culls triangles that must draw; snap the test to the active sample pattern or skip the stage when the pass is not single-sample and non-conservative — the one rung whose correctness depends on pipeline state, and it passes every single-sample test. (b) Bindless bullet extended: the material and page IDs this pipeline indexes with are per-pixel, not per-wave, so a non-wave-uniform descriptor index must be wrapped in `NonUniformResourceIndex()` (D3D12) / `nonuniformEXT` (SPIR-V), or the compiler may assume uniformity and broadcast one lane's index to the wave — the bug that renders correctly on one vendor and ships.
column4: Coverage-rule derivation. Single-sample: coverage at the pixel centre, so bounds enclosing no centre generate no fragment and the cull is exact. MSAA: sample positions are offset from the centre (the standard N-sample patterns place no sample at the centre for N>=2 in D3D's standard positions), so a sliver can cover a sample while missing the centre — culling it removes real coverage, and the loss lands on edges, which is where MSAA exists. Conservative raster: coverage is any overlap of the pixel square, a strict superset of the centre test, so the centre test culls primitives the rasterizer would have drawn. VRS: the inherited draft asserted the test is likewise wrong under coarse-rate VRS. Re-derived and NOT kept as stated — VRS changes the SHADING rate, not the coverage rule, so the pixel-grid coverage test still holds; the clause was rewritten to say the test survives and that the trap is deriving it from the shading rate instead. The audit records G7 as PLAUSIBLE (critic-reported, not independently confirmed), which is consistent with trimming the one sub-claim that does not follow from the coverage rule. NonUniformResourceIndex: descriptor indexing outside the wave-uniform case is undefined without the intrinsic in both D3D12 SM6.x and SPIR-V; spelling of both intrinsics checked.

column3: Prefix-sum bullet: the front-to-back claim removed, the determinism half kept and sharpened. Before: "Prefix-sum compaction gives ordered survivor lists — front-to-back for early-Z, deterministic for capture comparison". After: prefix-sum compaction preserves the survivors' INPUT order, which append does not, so the list is deterministic frame to frame and capture comparison works; it does NOT give front-to-back, because input order is the scene buffer's order and that is view-independent; early-Z ordering needs a view-dependent sort or a depth-bucket pass after compaction. The "worth it once counts reach hundreds of thousands" threshold kept, with "or as soon as you need bit-exact captures" added.
column4: Textual/algebraic. A prefix-sum compaction writes survivor i to offset = exclusive_scan(pass_flag)[i], a monotonically non-decreasing function of the input index, so output order is the restriction of input order to survivors — an order fixed by the scene buffer's layout, which no camera term enters. Atomic append orders by the nondeterministic arrival of atomic increments, which is why append loses determinism. Front-to-back requires a key derived from view-space depth, i.e. a view-dependent sort or a bucketing pass; neither is implied by a scan. Matches the audit's X21 (LOW, CHECKED) exactly, including its note that the determinism half is correct.

column3: The runtime scheduler is now stated ONCE, under `## When the user drags a slider`, and every other mention points at it instead of restating a competing absolute. The policy: fixed `dt <= dt_stable`; each frame add elapsed wall time to an accumulator and CLAMP THE ACCUMULATOR to `N_max*dt`; consume whole `dt` ticks; keep the sub-`dt` remainder. Two paragraphs carry the consequences: (a) what the clamp discards is sim-time LAG, not physics -- every tick taken is a full legal step, the lag is dropped and never repaid, so the cap binding IS the crossover table's slow-motion row rather than a second policy competing with it; the alternative (keep the debt, pay it at N_max ticks a frame) fast-forwards after every hitch and spirals; (b) determinism is TICK determinism -- state after tick k is a deterministic function of the tick count provided inputs are keyed to ticks, and ticks per wall-second are equal across machines only at or above `1/(N_max*dt)`. Rewritten to the same words: `## Use this`'s Runtime bullet (:49-53), the decision-rule `N` small row, and the crossover table's Substeps / When the budget runs out / Determinism rows. Determinism row softened from 'reproducible *and* independent of frame rate' to 'reproducible run-to-run for the same tick sequence, inputs keyed to ticks; ticks per wall-second equal across machines only at or above `1/(N_max*dt)` fps, by construction'. Failure table: three rows rewritten and two added -- 'a hitch, then the water runs fast-forward for a second' (accumulator unclamped, debt repaid) and 'two machines diverge from the same inputs' (an input keyed to a frame or to wall time). PLAN v1's 'discard beyond' wording is NOT used; Revision 2 overrides it. [fiedler_timestep] kept, with the honest note that the clamp is his max-frame-time guard put on the sum rather than on the sample -- same bound, stated on the quantity actually spent, so N_max IS the most ticks one frame can take.

column4: Derived and then measured here, independently of shallow-water.md. Derivation: flux update df/dt = (gA/l)*dH per one-way pipe; with both pipes on a face the net face flux F obeys dF/dt = 2*(gA/l)*(H_i - H_j); continuity dd_i/dt = (F_in - F_out)/dx^2; eliminating F gives d2d/dt2 = 2*(gA/l)*d2d/dx2, so c = sqrt(2*g*A/l). The staggered (leapfrog) update in 2-D is bounded by dt <= dx/(c*sqrt(2)) = dx/(2*sqrt(g*A/l)) = 0.50*dx/sqrt(g*A/l). Measurement: scratchpad/verify-timebudget/b1_counts.py and b3_tick.py (the originally named harness was never in the repo, which is how two wrong numbers survived) section (2) bisects dt_crit on a 32^2 grid with the max(0,.) and the outflow clamp both DISABLED so instability is visible; dt_crit/(dx/sqrt(g*A/l)) = 0.5006 for (dx,A,l,depth) = (1,1,1,1), (1,4,1,1), (1,1,4,1), (2,1,1,1), (1,1,1,10) and (2,4,2,0.1) -- flat in all four, matching shallow-water.md's independently measured 0.502 and the 0.1604 entry in its published-A table (0.502/sqrt(9.81) = 0.1603). column4: PLAN.md Revision 2 rules out the v1 gate `w'_i = (w_i > 0) ? ... : 0`; re-derived here and confirmed wrong for the stated reason. With w unnormalised, `b_i = w_i + h_i` scores an absent material at h_i alone against a present one at w_j + h_j, so a zero-weight material wins whenever h_i > max_j(w_j + h_j) - depth -- likelier the smaller Sum w is, which is why the leak grows as the producer under-subscribes. Measured (200k texels, 3 materials, h ~ U(0,1)^3, weights Dirichlet-flat over the two present materials): printed form leaks into the w = 0 material in 5.119% of texels at Sum w = 1.0 / depth 0.1, 8.669% at depth 0.2, 12.413%/18.529% at Sum w = 0.7, 19.302%/27.246% at Sum w = 0.5, max share 1.0000 -- the audit's 28.7% at Sum w = 0.5 reproduces as 27.2% at depth 0.2 on this rig; its 0.95% at Sum w = 1.0 reads 5.1% here, a weight-distribution difference, not a disagreement about the mechanism. The v1 gate is identical to the printed form wherever the weight is small but nonzero, which is one texel inside every bilinear edge: at w_A = 1e-3, 5.123% (Sum w = 1, depth 0.1) and 8.725% (depth 0.2) of texels still take > 1% share, the same three figures as the ungated form; at w_A = 1e-2, 5.591% / 9.394%. The gate also creates a step at exactly zero (share 0.500000 at w_A = 1e-12, 0.000000 at w_A = 0) that bilinear filtering cannot produce -- the artefact X57 says does not exist. The weight-scaled bias removes both by construction, not statistically: after line 1 Sum w = 1, so max_j w_j >= 1/n and max_j b_j >= 1/n; with h in [0,1] (which the document already requires of height channels) b_i = w_i(1+h_i) <= 2 w_i, so 2 w_i <= 1/n - depth forces b_i <= max_j b_j - depth and w'_i = 0. Hence for depth < 1/n every material below (1/n - depth)/2 of the normalised weight is provably absent: 0.1167 at n = 3, depth 0.1; 0.0750 at n = 4, depth 0.1; no guarantee once depth >= 1/n. column4: Derived twice, independently, and the two agree. (1) ANALYTIC MOMENTS. For Tessendorf's choppy displacement the gradient matrix is M_ab = sum Re[(k_a k_b/|k|) h~ e^{ikx}], a zero-mean Gaussian matrix whose covariances are pure direction averages of the SAME spectral measure that gives the slope: with mss the total mean-square slope, isotropic gives Var(Mxx) = Var(Myy) = (3/8)mss, Var(Mxy) = Cov(Mxx,Myy) = (1/8)mss; a cos² directional spread gives (5/8, 1/8, 1/8, 1/8). J = 1 + q(Mxx+Myy) + q²(Mxx Myy - Mxy²) therefore depends on q only through s = q sqrt(mss), so the fold fraction is a function of s ALONE and the spectrum's radial shape drops out. 8e6-sample Monte Carlo: s_p = 0.7383 / 0.5734 / 0.4585 at p = 5% / 1% / 0.1% isotropic, 0.6943 / 0.5141 / 0.3956 under cos². Radial spectral slope moves s_p by less than the seed scatter; DIRECTIONAL SPREADING is what moves it, by 6-17%, which is why the printed pair is the cos² value with the unspread band named. The audit's critic value (q* x rms-slope = 0.534-0.542) and the plan's 0.52/0.41/0.70 both sit inside this band; the plan's triple is the cos² case to two digits. Single-wave sanity check: one trochoid folds at q a k = 1 and has mss = (ak)²/2, so s = 1/sqrt(2) = 0.707 at the first fold, and the Stokes limit ak = 0.44 needs q = 2.3 - both as the audit states. ⚠️ REPAIR DERIVATION (a third route, independent of the sitting's two): the invariance is provable, not just measured. MEASURED, 6 octaves, lacunarity 2, gain 0.5, P = 1024, integer per-octave offsets: with the prescribed 1024-entry table octave l repeats at 1024/2^l cells to 2.7e-13 - 3.1e-13 for l = 1..5, so octaves 1-5 summed are bit-identical at a 512-cell shift, max diff 3.95e-13 (printed as 4.0e-13); the detail band's peak is 0.305 against the full field's 0.656, and its amplitude weight is sum(0.5^k, k=1..5)/sum(0.5^k, k=0..5) = 0.96875/1.96875 = 0.492. With a 32768-entry hash (= P*lacunarity^5) the same band differs by 4.615e-01 at that shift (printed 4.6e-01) and no octave repeats at any shift <= 512. The wrap test at T = P reads 6.3e-13 (1024-entry) and 5.4e-13 (32768-entry) and passes in both cases. A 256-entry table, for reference, makes the whole field periodic at 256 cells.

column4: Operation tally written out and auditable (repair-seamless-noise/r4_simplex_cost.py). Per corner in d dimensions: d offset subtractions + (d mul + d sub) for the falloff argument + 2 mul for t^4 + (d mul + (d-1) add) for the gradient dot + 1 mul = 5d+2, i.e. 12 in 2-D and 22 in 4-D. Whole kernel: skew 2d + floor d + unskew 3d + d(d-1)/2 comparisons to rank the simplex + corners*(5d+2) + corners for the sum and scale = 52 at d = 2 with 3 corners and 145 at d = 4 with 5 corners, ratio 2.79. The embedding adds 6 mul/add-class ops and 4 TRANSCENDENTALS (2 sin, 2 cos) counted separately. Wall clock on the same machine, same vectorised style, 2^21 samples: 2-D 331 ms against 4-D-plus-embedding 1117 ms, 3.37x.

column4: Perspective projection: a world displacement v at camera-space depth z projects to (K/z)*v_perp for a near-axis point. With v = e*up, |v_perp| = e*sin(theta), theta = angle(view ray, world up). sin(theta)=1 at the horizon (maximum), 0 looking straight down. So e*K/d is the supremum over view orientation. Noted but NOT written into the document: at the extreme frustum corner the off-axis radial term (x*v_z/z) can exceed the centre value, so it is a worst case in ORIENTATION rather than a strict bound over the whole frustum -- the document therefore says 'orientation-independent worst case', not 'upper bound'. CORRECTED BY REPAIR: the 'noted but NOT written into the document' concession was the defect. The old prose called the maximum 'cheap and conservative' and told an engineer that measured error above prediction means a broken metric -- which inverts exactly where it matters. Re-derived: for a camera-space error v at (x,y,z) the first-order projected length is (K/z)*|v_xy - (x,y)*v_z/z|; maximising over unit v gives the largest singular value of [[1,0,-tx],[0,1,-ty]] = sqrt(1+tx^2+ty^2), and with d/z = sqrt(1+tx^2+ty^2) the max of actual/rho at a screen point is exactly 1 + tx^2 + ty^2 = 1 + tan^2(fovY/2)*(1+aspect^2). At 16:9 that is 2.387 / 5.161 / 9.486 at fovY 60/90/110. Brute-force check (41x41 frustum sweep x 4000 sampled orientations, |P| = 1000 m, e = 1 m) gives 2.389 / 5.171 / 9.513, the excess being the O(e/d) finite-difference term. Two named orientations: horizon max = sqrt(1+tx^2+ty^2) = 1.545 / 2.272 / 3.080; looking straight down max = sqrt(1+tx^2+ty^2)*sqrt(tx^2+ty^2) = 1.822 / 4.644 / 9.000 -- so 'the projection falls to zero looking straight down' is an ON-AXIS statement only. The ratio does NOT disturb the crack section's tau-cancellation at :205-215, because crack and e are projected at the same point and the off-axis factor is common to both.

column4: Cutoff at X suppresses the rebuild of X's DEPENDENTS, so the saving is cost(cone), not cost(X); :176 states the corpus topology, 'the expensive nodes sit downstream of the cheap ones'. Expected cost with hashing = hash + (1-P)*cone; without = cone; equal at hash = P*cone, so hash iff cost(hash) < P*cost(cone). Checked numerically: at P = 0.005, 50 + 0.995*10000 = 10000.0 ms exactly, the two arms tie. Break-even on the page's own figures: sha256 on 4096^2 float32 = 50 ms, erosion cone taken at 10 s -> 50/10000 = 0.5%; at the 'minutes' the scheduler table quotes (:113) it falls to 50/60000 = 0.083%, so 10 s is the pessimistic end. The old node-local rule forbids hashing a clamp (clamp ~ copy = 15 ms < 50 ms hash) and the clamp is precisely the motivating example at :183-186; the new one requires it, clearing by 10000/50 = 200x at P^ = 1. DEVIATION FROM PLAN.md:169 AND THE REPLACEMENT-FIX CRITIC, recorded per Revision 2's rule: both ask for a structural prior 'near 1' for clamp/quantise/mask. Re-derived and NOT WRITTEN AS 'near 1'. The hash is over the WHOLE FIELD, so P(output unchanged) is the probability that not one of 16.7e6 cells moved. For a quantiser of step q under a perturbation of size eps that is ~(1-eps/q)^16.7e6, which is ~0 unless eps/q < 1e-8; for a clamp, a generic upstream nudge moves at least one unsaturated cell. P^ ~ 1 is true only where the WHOLE change lands in the destroyed region -- which is two of the document's three worked cases (a nudge clamped away, a result masked to zero; the third is a value in the eighth decimal place of a quantised parameter), and that is how it is now written: seed the information-destroying nodes high, P^ = 1 where the whole change lands in the destroyed region, seed bijective/reseeded nodes at 0. The operational consequence is identical -- both priors sit above the 0.5% bar, so both hash the clamp -- but the claim is now true. The structural asymmetry that survives is non-injectivity: a many-to-one operator has a positive-measure set of input changes mapping to one output; a bijection or a reseeded noise node has none.

column3: REVISED AFTER VERIFICATION -- the original claim named one threshold where the specification permits three. ORIGINAL: |x| <= 2^-12.5 = 1.726e-4 squares to zero in binary16, so a 2- or 3-vector there has dot(v,v) == 0 and normalize is 0/0; and (WRONG) 'that is 2.83x above the smallest normal, so denormal flush-to-zero never enters the story'. CORRECTED: [d3d11spec] 7.20.2.2.1 says float16 MIN-PRECISION arithmetic 'may or may not flush float16 denorm to 0, and may either round to nearest even or truncate to a representable number', which permits three regimes with three thresholds. Component bound, largest value there, slope, height across a 2 m cell: |x| <= 2^-12.5 -> 1.7262e-4, 0.0099 deg, 0.35 mm (round to nearest even, subnormals preserved); |x| < 2^-12 -> 2.4402e-4, 0.0140 deg, 0.49 mm (truncating, 1.41x); |x| < 2^-7 -> 7.8087e-3, 0.447 deg, 15.6 mm (subnormal PRODUCTS flushed, 45.2x). The document now states 1.726e-4 as the FLOOR and sizes the hazard at 7.8e-3.
column4: Squares are lost at or below 2^-25 under round-to-nearest-even (half the smallest subnormal, the tie going to the even significand, which is zero), below 2^-24 under truncation, and below the smallest NORMAL 2^-14 where subnormal results are flushed -- 2^10 sooner. Square-root each for the component bound. Confirmed by an exhaustive sweep over all 31743 positive finite binary16 bit patterns under each regime (scratchpad/repair-shader-craft/fp16_regimes.py, written here and independent of the verifier's): largest value giving dot(v,v) == 0 is 1.726151e-4 (log2 -12.5002), 2.440214e-4 (log2 -12.0007) and 7.808685e-3 (log2 -7.0007), identical for a 2-vector and a 3-vector, and the flush threshold is the same under either rounding mode (checked). THE NARROW CLAIM THAT SURVIVES: every threshold is 2.83x to 128x ABOVE the smallest normal 2^-14, so each COMPONENT is an ordinary normal number and the collapse is never an artefact of denormal INPUTS. What flushing decides is the fate of the PRODUCTS, which are subnormal by construction.
column5: Boundary demonstration corrected at the same end: at 2^-12 the three squares sum to 3*2^-24 = 1.788e-7 and the normalize succeeds ONLY where float16 denorms are preserved. 2^-24 is itself the smallest subnormal, so under flush-to-zero each product goes to zero alone, the sum is 0.0 and the normalize fails there too -- measured, not argued. A SECOND spec section the verifier did not report was read here and is load-bearing: 7.20.2.2.1 governs MIN-precision float16 (min16float, and GLSL ES mediump by the same logic), while 3.1.5 MANDATES round-to-nearest-even at 0.5 ULP and 'Denorms: 16-bit floating point numbers must preserve denorms' for FULL float16. So the three-regime span is real for exactly the type the document names at lines 336 and in the failure row, and NOT for native half -- which is why the correction is a widening and not a retraction. Both sections entered in papers-rendering.md before the prose citing them (RULE 7).

column3: New claim, the cross-API divergence: HLSL saturate(NaN) is 0 by [d3d11spec] 22.19.1, which defines _sat as min(1.0f, max(0.0f, value)) over the min/max INSTRUCTIONS of 22.10.11 and 22.10.10, which return the other operand when one is NaN -- the spec's own sentence is 'sat(NaN) returns 0, by the rules for min and max'.
